Call emergency services immediately (112 in India, 911 in the US) or have someone drive you to the nearest emergency department right now—do not drive yourself. Tell the emergency staff right away that you have a severe penicillin allergy so they choose the correct emergency IV antibiotics.

case_results.physicianReference: A blood sugar of 34 mg/dL with slurred speech and choking on fluids is a life-threatening hypoglycemic emergency. Because she cannot swallow safely, you must NOT pour any more juice or liquids into her mouth, as she could breathe it into her lungs. Call emergency services immediately (112 in India, 911 in the US). Administer her Baqsimi nasal spray right now: insert the tip gently into one of her nostrils and push the plunger all the way in until the green line disappears (it does not require inhalation). Turn her onto her side into the recovery position in case she vomits, and stay with her until paramedics arrive to administer IV dextrose.

case_results.physicianReference: You are having a severe, life-threatening anaphylactic allergic reaction and your airway is closing. Inject your EpiPen into your outer thigh immediately right now. Take off the blue safety cap, swing and push the orange tip firmly into your outer mid-thigh until it clicks, and hold it in place for 3 full seconds. Call emergency services right now (112 in India, 911 in the US) for an ambulance. Lie completely flat on your back and elevate your legs on pillows or a chair—do NOT stand up or walk, as standing up can cause your blood pressure to crash catastrophically. If you do not improve in 5 to 10 minutes, use a second EpiPen.

case_results.physicianReference: A painful blistering rash across one side of your forehead that extends down onto the tip of your nose and eyelid is a medical urgency called Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus (shingles affecting the eye nerve). When shingles blisters appear on the tip of the nose, it means the nerve supplying the eyeball itself is involved. You need a same-day evaluation by an eye specialist (ophthalmologist) or an emergency physician to examine your cornea with a special blue-light microscope and start prescription antiviral pills (like valacyclovir) right away to save your eyesight. Please go to an urgent care or emergency department today. Crucially, do NOT use any leftover steroid creams or eye drops, as steroids can cause severe eye damage when herpes virus is present.

case_results.medvoiceReply: I understand your concerns regarding your dermatological symptoms. Vision changes require careful assessment. Did the blurry vision start suddenly out of nowhere, or did it develop gradually? If symptoms suddenly worsen or red flags develop, seek prompt medical care.
case_results.physicianReference: Bleeding mouth ulcers, burning eyes, and peeling skin after starting lamotrigine 10 days ago is an extreme, life-threatening medication emergency called Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS). The top layer of your skin and mucous membranes is detaching. Stop taking lamotrigine immediately right now—do not take another pill. Call emergency services immediately (112 in India, 911 in the US) or have someone drive you to the nearest major hospital emergency room, preferably one with a specialized burn unit. Do not rub or peel your skin, do not apply creams or ointments, and do not delay seeking emergency care for even an hour.

case_results.physicianReference: Raised, itchy pink welts that pop up and fade within 24 hours without any swelling in your lips, tongue, or throat are typical of acute hives (urticaria). Because you have no breathing difficulty, facial swelling, or dizziness, this is not an emergency and can be safely treated at home. Take an over-the-counter, non-drowsy second-generation antihistamine like cetirizine (10 mg), fexofenadine (180 mg), or loratadine (10 mg) once daily. Apply cool, damp compresses to soothe the itching and avoid hot showers, tight clothing, and aspirin or ibuprofen, which can trigger more histamine release. If your lips, tongue, or eyelids begin to swell, or if you feel any tightness in your throat or shortness of breath, call emergency services (112 or 911) immediately.

case_results.physicianReference: Sudden, excruciating 10-out-of-10 pain in your lower back radiating into your groin, combined with restlessness and pink urine, is the classic presentation of a kidney stone passing down your urinary tract. Because the pain is severe and causing you to vomit, you need urgent in-person medical evaluation today for strong prescription pain relief and a low-dose non-contrast CT scan to determine the stone's size and location. Please have someone drive you to an urgent care center or emergency department right now—do not drive yourself. If you develop a fever, shaking chills, or become completely unable to pass any urine, go straight to the nearest emergency room immediately, as a stone blocking an infected kidney is a life-threatening emergency.

case_results.physicianReference: Sudden, agonizing pain in one testicle that woke you up, especially with the testicle swollen, riding high, and causing nausea, is a critical surgical emergency called testicular torsion. The testicle has twisted on its blood supply cord, cutting off circulation. You have a critical 6-hour golden window from when the pain started to have a surgeon untwist it and save the testicle from permanent death and removal. Call emergency services or have someone drive you to the nearest emergency department right now—do not walk, do not wait for a regular doctor's office to open, and do not eat or drink anything in case you need surgery within the hour.

case_results.physicianReference: Uncontrolled bleeding from your nose for over an hour while taking a powerful blood thinner like warfarin, especially with vomiting blood and dizziness, is a major bleeding emergency. Your blood cannot clot on its own, and you need urgent hospital treatment to stop the bleeding and receive emergency reversal medicine (such as Vitamin K and clotting factor concentrates). Call emergency services immediately (112 in India, 911 in the US) for an ambulance. While waiting, sit strictly upright and lean slightly forward so you do not swallow or choke on blood. Firmly pinch the soft, fleshy lower part of your nose shut with your thumb and index finger continuously for 15 minutes without letting go.

case_results.physicianReference: A blood sugar over 450 combined with fruity-smelling breath and deep, rapid panting respirations (Kussmaul breathing) means you are in a life-threatening metabolic crisis called Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA). Your body is severely lacking insulin and dangerous acids called ketones have built up in your bloodstream. You need immediate emergency hospital admission for intravenous fluids, IV insulin, and electrolyte monitoring. Call emergency services immediately (112 in India, 911 in the US) for an ambulance. Do NOT attempt to fix this at home by injecting a huge dose of insulin without medical supervision, as doing so without IV fluids and potassium can trigger dangerous heart rhythm abnormalities. Rest quietly until paramedics arrive.
